Pool a prespecified linear analysis of completed datasets

Source: R/analysis.R
catmech_pool_lm.Rd

Uses Rubin's scalar rules with the complete-data residual degrees of freedom. A result is conditional on the imputation/analysis models and their assumptions. Failed convergence is rejected. The legacy retain/replace sensitivity engine requires explicit opt-in and is labeled as sensitivity output.

Usage

catmech_pool_lm(
  result,
  formula,
  conf_level = 0.95,
  allow_sensitivity = FALSE,
  cluster = NULL,
  cluster_variance = c("cv3", "cr1s")
)

Arguments

result

A catmech_result from [catmech_model()], [catmech_pmm()], [catmech_reference()], [catmech_contamination()] or [catmech_impute()].

formula

A prespecified formula for [stats::lm()]. Missing analysis values are rejected rather than silently dropping records.

conf_level

Confidence level between zero and one.

allow_sensitivity

Explicitly allow pooled calculations for the legacy sensitivity engine or experimental partial-reference PMM. Results retain a sensitivity-only label; this does not establish their inferential validity.

cluster

Optional name of a complete column in the completed data identifying clusters. Each completed analysis then uses a cluster-robust variance, pooled by Rubin's rules with complete-data degrees of freedom of clusters minus one. A fit from `catmech_reference(cluster = )` uses its own column by default. With few clusters, or a few influential ones, these intervals can be too narrow. A coefficient determined by a single cluster, such as a site type found at one site, draws a warning, because its interval can be far too narrow. This variance repairs the analysis step only: linear imputation without `cluster` still undercovered on real items after it.

cluster_variance

With `cluster`, `"cv3"` (the default) for the delete-one-cluster jackknife, or `"cr1s"` for the form with factor (G / (G - 1)) ((n - 1) / (n - p)), the default through version 0.6.0. A planned test chose `"cv3"`, narrowly, as documented in `validation/VARIANCE_MI_SYNTHESIS.md`. It gives wider intervals than `"cr1s"`.

Value

A data.frame with term, estimate, std.error, df, lower, upper, within_variance, between_variance, m, n and interpretation, plus clusters when a cluster-robust variance was used.

Details

When every audited row agreed and recorded values were kept, the interpretation ends in `_recorded_kept`, and a warning repeats that those records are treated as correct. When the workflow declares that no target cells were imputed, all completed analysis frames must agree and ordinary complete-data t intervals are returned. A zero estimated between-imputation variance alone does not activate this rule. Predictive matching and reference-subset results retain distinct interpretation labels; none guarantees coverage under misspecification. Partial-reference PMM requires explicit sensitivity opt-in because held-out studies found material undercoverage even with random accurate references. This package policy does not assert that every PMM application is invalid. Only univariate linear models with at least one named coefficient are supported.

Examples

set.seed(123)
n <- 40
df <- data.frame(
  lab = stats::rnorm(n, 10, 2),
  age = stats::rnorm(n, 50, 10),
  outcome = stats::rnorm(n, 5, 1)
)
df$lab_ref <- df$lab
df$lab_ref[11:n] <- NA
res <- catmech_reference(df, value = "lab", reference = "lab_ref",
                         predictors = "age", m = 2, seed = 1)
pooled <- catmech_pool_lm(res, outcome ~ lab + age)
print(pooled)
#> -- Catmech Pooled Linear Model --
#> Completions (m): 2 | Observations (n): 40
#> 
#>         term estimate std.error      df   lower  upper
#>  (Intercept)   5.4865    0.9781 25.8621  3.4755 7.4975
#>          lab   0.0130    0.0795 15.1264 -0.1562 0.1823
#>          age  -0.0121    0.0145 35.0956 -0.0415 0.0173
#>               interpretation
#>  conditional_reference_model
#>  conditional_reference_model
#>  conditional_reference_model
